title: The future of electric cars
paragraphs: We are all aware of the damaging pollution that’s created by driving petrol and diesel vehicles. Many of the world’s cities are clogged with traffic, creating fumes containing gases such as nitrogen oxides. The solution for a cleaner, greener future could be electric vehicles. But how optimistic should we be?

There was much excitement last year when the UK government announced it will ban the sale of new petrol and diesel cars from 2030. But is that easier said than done? The road to global traffic being totally electric is still a long way off. Currently, battery life is an issue – a fully charged battery won’t take you as far as a full tank of petrol. There are also limited numbers of charging points to plug an EV into.

Of course, technology is always improving. Some of the biggest tech companies, like Google and Tesla, are spending huge amounts of money developing electric cars. And most of the big car manufacturers are now making them too. Colin Herron, a consultant on low-carbon vehicle technology, told the BBC: “The big leap forward will come with solid state batteries, which will appear first in mobile phones and laptops before they progress to cars.” These will charge more quickly and give cars a bigger range.

Cost is another issue that may deter people switching to electric power. But some countries offer incentives, such as cutting prices by reducing import taxes, and not charging for road tax and parking. Some also provide exclusive lanes for electric cars to be driven on, overtaking traditional cars which might be stuck in jams. These kinds of measures have made Norway the country with the most electric cars per capita at more than thirty electric cars per 1000 inhabitants.

But Colin Herron warns that ‘electric motoring’ doesn’t mean a zero-carbon future. “It’s emission-free motoring, but the car has to be built, the battery has to be built, and the electricity does come from somewhere.” Maybe it’s time to think about making fewer journeys or using public transport.

vocabulary.entry: petrol vehicle /ˈpetrəl ˈviːəkl/ n. 汽油车
vocabulary.example: The petrol vehicle is still popular in some developing areas.
vocabulary.translation: 汽油车在一些发展中地区依然很受欢迎。

vocabulary.entry: diesel vehicle /ˈdiːzl ˈviːəkl/ n. 柴油车
vocabulary.example: This diesel vehicle is designed for long-distance transportation.
vocabulary.translation: 这款柴油车是为长途运输设计的。

vocabulary.entry: clog /klɒɡ/ v. 堵塞；阻塞
vocabulary.example: The drain was clogged with hair and dirt.
vocabulary.translation: 排水管道被头发和污垢堵塞了。

vocabulary.entry: fume /fjuːm/ n. 尾气；烟雾
vocabulary.example: The factory chimneys emitted thick black fumes.
vocabulary.translation: 工厂的烟囱排放出浓浓的黑烟。

vocabulary.entry: nitrogen oxide /ˈnaɪtrədʒən ˈɒksaɪd/ n. 氮氧化物
vocabulary.example: Nitrogen oxide is one of the main pollutants in vehicle exhaust.
vocabulary.translation: 氮氧化物是汽车尾气中的主要污染物之一。

vocabulary.entry: electric vehicle /ɪˈlektrɪk ˈviːəkl/ n. 电动汽车（缩写为EV）
vocabulary.example: Many people choose to buy an electric vehicle to reduce carbon footprint.
vocabulary.translation: 很多人选择购买电动汽车来减少碳足迹。

vocabulary.entry: ban /bæn/ v. 禁止；取缔
vocabulary.example: The government decided to ban smoking in all public places.
vocabulary.translation: 政府决定在所有公共场所禁烟。

vocabulary.term: easier said than done 说起来容易做起来难
vocabulary.entry: easier said than done 说起来容易做起来难
vocabulary.example: Losing weight is easier said than done for most people.
vocabulary.translation: 对大多数人来说，减肥都是说起来容易做起来难。

vocabulary.entry: battery life /ˈbætri laɪf/ n. 电池续航能力
vocabulary.example: The battery life of this smartphone can last up to two days.
vocabulary.translation: 这款智能手机的电池续航能力可达两天。

vocabulary.entry: tank /tæŋk/ n. （车辆的）油箱
vocabulary.example: He filled the tank with petrol before starting the long journey.
vocabulary.translation: 他在开始长途旅行前把油箱加满了汽油。

vocabulary.entry: charging point /ˈtʃɑːdʒɪŋ pɔɪnt/ n. 充电桩
vocabulary.example: I couldn't find a charging point for my electric car in the remote area.
vocabulary.translation: 我在那个偏远地区找不到电动汽车的充电桩。

vocabulary.entry: plug into /plʌɡ ˈɪntuː/ 接入；插入充电
vocabulary.example: You need to plug the device into a power source to charge it.
vocabulary.translation: 你需要把这个设备接入电源才能充电。

vocabulary.entry: manufacturer /ˌmænjuˈfæktʃərə/ n. 制造商；生产商
vocabulary.example: The car manufacturer launched a new model of electric vehicle this year.
vocabulary.translation: 这家汽车制造商今年推出了一款新的电动汽车车型。

vocabulary.entry: low-carbon /ˌləʊ ˈkɑːbən/ adj. 低碳的
vocabulary.example: We should promote low-carbon lifestyles to protect the environment.
vocabulary.translation: 我们应该倡导低碳生活方式来保护环境。

vocabulary.entry: solid state battery /ˈsɒlɪd steɪt ˈbætri/ n. 固态电池
vocabulary.example: The solid state battery is expected to revolutionize the electric vehicle industry.
vocabulary.translation: 固态电池有望给电动汽车行业带来革命性变化。

vocabulary.entry: leap forward /liːp ˈfɔːwəd/ n. 飞跃；长足进步
vocabulary.example: The invention of the internet marked a great leap forward in communication.
vocabulary.translation: 互联网的发明标志着通信领域的一次巨大飞跃。

vocabulary.entry: range /reɪndʒ/ n. （车辆的）续航里程
vocabulary.example: The new electric car has a range of over 500 kilometers on a single charge.
vocabulary.translation: 这款新电动汽车单次充电续航里程超过500公里。

vocabulary.entry: deter /dɪˈtɜː/ v. 阻止；打消……的念头
vocabulary.example: The high cost didn't deter him from buying the luxury watch.
vocabulary.translation: 高昂的价格并没有打消他购买这款奢侈品手表的念头。

vocabulary.entry: incentive /ɪnˈsentɪv/ n. 激励措施；奖励
vocabulary.example: The government provides tax incentives to encourage business investment.
vocabulary.translation: 政府提供税收优惠作为激励措施，鼓励企业投资。

vocabulary.entry: import tax /ˈɪmpɔːt tæks/ n. 进口税
vocabulary.example: The country reduced the import tax on electric vehicles to boost sales.
vocabulary.translation: 该国降低了电动汽车的进口税，以促进销量增长。

vocabulary.entry: road tax /rəʊd tæks/ n. 道路税；车辆使用税
vocabulary.example: Owners of electric vehicles are exempt from paying road tax in this city.
vocabulary.translation: 这座城市的电动汽车车主无需缴纳道路税。

vocabulary.entry: exclusive lane /ɪkˈskluːsɪv leɪn/ n. 专用车道
vocabulary.example: The city built an exclusive lane for bicycles to ensure their safety.
vocabulary.translation: 这座城市专门修建了自行车专用车道，以保障骑行者的安全。

vocabulary.entry: overtake /ˌəʊvəˈteɪk/ v. 超车；超过
vocabulary.example: The sports car overtook all the other vehicles on the highway.
vocabulary.translation: 这辆跑车在高速公路上超过了其他所有车辆。

vocabulary.entry: per capita /pə ˈkæpɪtə/ adv. 人均；按人头计算
vocabulary.example: The country has a high income per capita compared to its neighbors.
vocabulary.translation: 与邻国相比，这个国家的人均收入很高。

vocabulary.entry: emission-free /ɪˈmɪʃn friː/ adj. 零排放的
vocabulary.example: Emission-free public transport is essential for building a green city.
vocabulary.translation: 零排放公共交通对于建设绿色城市至关重要。

sentences.english: We are all aware of the damaging pollution that’s created by driving petrol and diesel vehicles.
sentences.chinese: 我们都清楚，驾驶汽油车和柴油车会产生有害污染。

sentences.english: Many of the world’s cities are clogged with traffic, creating fumes containing gases such as nitrogen oxides.
sentences.chinese: 世界上许多城市都被交通拥堵所困扰，车辆排放的尾气中含有氮氧化物等气体。

sentences.english: The solution for a cleaner, greener future could be electric vehicles.
sentences.chinese: 想要实现更清洁、更环保的未来，电动汽车或许是一个解决方案。

sentences.english: But how optimistic should we be?
sentences.chinese: 但我们对此应该持多乐观的态度呢？

sentences.english: There was much excitement last year when the UK government announced it will ban the sale of new petrol and diesel cars from 2030.
sentences.chinese: 去年英国政府宣布将从2030年起禁止销售新的汽油车和柴油车时，人们都感到十分振奋。

sentences.english: But is that easier said than done?
sentences.chinese: 但这件事真的是说起来容易做起来难吗？

sentences.english: The road to global traffic being totally electric is still a long way off.
sentences.chinese: 要实现全球交通全面电动化，还有很长的路要走。

sentences.english: Currently, battery life is an issue – a fully charged battery won’t take you as far as a full tank of petrol.
sentences.chinese: 目前，电池续航能力是一大问题——一块充满电的电池，续航里程远不及一箱汽油。

sentences.english: There are also limited numbers of charging points to plug an EV into.
sentences.chinese: 此外，可供电动汽车充电的充电桩数量也十分有限。

sentences.english: Of course, technology is always improving.
sentences.chinese: 当然，技术一直在不断进步。

sentences.english: Some of the biggest tech companies, like Google and Tesla, are spending huge amounts of money developing electric cars. And most of the big car manufacturers are now making them too.
sentences.chinese: 谷歌、特斯拉等大型科技公司都在投入巨资研发电动汽车，大多数主流汽车制造商如今也开始生产电动汽车。

sentences.english: Colin Herron, a consultant on low-carbon vehicle technology, told the BBC: “The big leap forward will come with solid state batteries, which will appear first in mobile phones and laptops before they progress to cars.”
sentences.chinese: 低碳汽车技术顾问科林·赫伦在接受BBC采访时表示：“固态电池的出现将会带来巨大的技术飞跃，这类电池会率先应用于手机和笔记本电脑，之后才会推广到汽车领域。”

sentences.english: These will charge more quickly and give cars a bigger range.
sentences.chinese: 固态电池充电速度更快，还能为汽车带来更长的续航里程。

sentences.english: Cost is another issue that may deter people switching to electric power.
sentences.chinese: 成本是另一个可能阻碍人们转向电动汽车的因素。

sentences.english: But some countries offer incentives, such as cutting prices by reducing import taxes, and not charging for road tax and parking.
sentences.chinese: 但一些国家推出了激励政策，比如通过降低进口税来压低车价，免除车辆的道路税和停车费。

sentences.english: Some also provide exclusive lanes for electric cars to be driven on, overtaking traditional cars which might be stuck in jams.
sentences.chinese: 部分国家还专门设置了电动汽车专用车道，让电动汽车可以超越那些可能陷入拥堵的传统燃油车。

sentences.english: These kinds of measures have made Norway the country with the most electric cars per capita at more than thirty electric cars per 1000 inhabitants.
sentences.chinese: 这类政策让挪威成为了人均电动汽车拥有量最高的国家，每1000名居民所拥有的电动汽车数量超过30辆。

sentences.english: But Colin Herron warns that ‘electric motoring’ doesn’t mean a zero-carbon future.
sentences.chinese: 但科林·赫伦提醒道，“电动汽车出行”并不意味着零碳未来。

sentences.english: “It’s emission-free motoring, but the car has to be built, the battery has to be built, and the electricity does come from somewhere.”
sentences.chinese: “电动汽车行驶时确实不会产生尾气排放，但汽车本身需要制造，电池也需要生产，而且电力也并非凭空而来。”

sentences.english: Maybe it’s time to think about making fewer journeys or using public transport.
sentences.chinese: 或许我们是时候考虑减少出行次数，或是多使用公共交通工具了。
